text.title: Incident Decision Template — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete incident decision record from a 02:14 checkout incident — sidecar disabled in eu-west-1, three options, quantified blast radius, numeric rollback trigger, pinned evidence, reviewed at the postmortem — with a note on each non-obvious value, and the same call written the way it usually is, with what the validator and the postmortem reviewer see.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: INC-2417, 2026-09-12 02:14 UTC. Checkout 5xx in eu-west-1 climbing since a release of the recommendations sidecar. Incident commander ic:alice decides on the bridge to disable the sidecar; sre:bob will run the command. The scribe types while she talks and commits at 02:15:40.

example.title: INC-2417 sidecar disable
example.note: `committed_at` is 100 seconds after `decided_at` with the bridge open, so no `reconstructed` entry is needed (r-record-before-bridge-closes). `owner` is the commander, and the engineer who ran `helm` is the `executor` entry, so the postmortem can see who decided and who typed (r-owner-is-commander-or-delegate). Three options including the do-nothing line with the reason it was rejected (r-options-considered-min-two). `blast_radius` carries a percentage, a request rate and the tenants that were not affected (r-blast-radius-quantified). `rollback_trigger` is four fields, each of which someone on the bridge could act on without asking (r-rollback-trigger-measurable). The Grafana link carries `from`/`to` in epoch milliseconds, and the Slack permalink shows the moment the decision was announced (r-evidence-is-timestamped-signal). `next_review_at` equals the postmortem date and `outcome` was filled there: the trigger never fired and the measured radius (36%) matched the recorded 38% (r-review-at-postmortem).

example.title: the same call as it is usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: `options_considered` has 1 item and none contains do nothing / keep observing (r-options-considered-min-two); `blast_radius` has no number (r-blast-radius-quantified); `rollback_trigger.threshold` and `window` carry no number (r-rollback-trigger-measurable); `decision` contains "should probably", "consider" and "look into" (r-decision-is-one-imperative-sentence); the Grafana URL has no pinned time range and the second URL is a runbook page (r-evidence-is-timestamped-signal); `next_review_at` is three months after the postmortem (r-review-at-postmortem). What the postmortem reviewer sees: the owner is the executor, so nobody can say who made the call (fm-06), and the dashboard link now shows a healthy system (fm-05).
